explanation.text:
An earnest cry for divine aid against his enemies, as being also those of God, is followed by the Psalmist's praise in assurance of a favorable answer, and a prayer for all God's people. (Psa 28:1-9)

my rock-- (Psa 18:2, Psa 18:31).

be not silent to me--literally, "from me," deaf or inattentive.

become like them, etc.--share their fate.

go down into the pit--or, "grave" (Psa 30:3).

bsb.title: Of David.
bsb.text: To You, O LORD, I call; be not deaf to me, O my Rock. For if You remain silent, I will be like those descending to the Pit.

explanation.text:
lift up my hands--a gesture of prayer (Psa 63:4; Psa 141:2).

oracle--place of speaking (Exo 25:22; Num 7:89), where God answered His people (compare Psa 5:7).

bsb.text: Hear my cry for mercy when I call to You for help, when I lift up my hands toward Your holy sanctuary.

explanation.text: Draw me not away--implies punishment as well as death (compare Psa 26:9). Hypocrisy is the special wickedness mentioned.

bsb.text: Do not drag me away with the wicked, and with the workers of iniquity, who speak peace to their neighbors while malice is in their hearts.

explanation.text:
The imprecation is justified in Psa 28:5. The force of the passage is greatly enhanced by the accumulation of terms describing their sin.

endeavours--points out their deliberate sinfulness.

bsb.text: Repay them according to their deeds and for their works of evil. Repay them for what their hands have done; bring back on them what they deserve.

explanation.text:
Disregard of God's judgments brings a righteous punishment.

destroy . . . build . . . up--The positive strengthened by the negative form.

bsb.text: Since they show no regard for the works of the LORD or what His hands have done, He will tear them down and never rebuild them.
Blessed be the LORD, for He has heard my cry for mercy.

explanation.text: The repetition of "heart" denotes his sincerity.

bsb.text: The LORD is my strength and my shield; my heart trusts in Him, and I am helped. Therefore my heart rejoices, and I give thanks to Him with my song.

explanation.text:
The distinction made between the people.

their strength--and the anointed--may indicate Absalom's rebellion as the occasion.

bsb.text: The LORD is the strength of His people, a stronghold of salvation for His anointed.

explanation.text:
The special prayer for the people sustains this view.

feed them--as a shepherd (Psa 23:1, etc.).

Next: Psalms Chapter 29

bsb.text: Save Your people and bless Your inheritance; shepherd them and carry them forever.
